stimulus.title: A nickel-copper cell
stimulus.html:
A student builds the galvanic cell shown. Beaker 1 holds a nickel strip in 1.0 M Ni(NO₃)₂(aq); Beaker 2 holds a copper strip in 1.0 M Cu(NO₃)₂(aq). The salt bridge contains KNO₃(aq). The temperature is 25 °C.

Standard reduction potentials at 25 °C
Half-reactionE° (V)
Cu²⁺(aq) + 2e⁻ → Cu(s)+0.34
Ni²⁺(aq) + 2e⁻ → Ni(s)−0.25

F = 96,485 C/mol e⁻; molar mass of Cu = 63.55 g/mol.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Identify the electrode at which oxidation occurs, and write the half-reaction that occurs there.

rubric.point: The nickel electrode (Beaker 1) is the anode, with Ni(s) → Ni²⁺(aq) + 2e⁻

parts.sample: Oxidation occurs at the nickel electrode, the anode: Ni(s) → Ni²⁺(aq) + 2e⁻. Ni²⁺/Ni has the lower reduction potential (−0.25 V), so nickel is the species oxidized.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Write the balanced net ionic equation for the overall reaction in the cell.

accept: Ni + Cu²⁺ → Ni²⁺ + Cu (state symbols not required)

parts.sample: Ni(s) + Cu²⁺(aq) → Ni²⁺(aq) + Cu(s). Two electrons are lost by Ni and two gained by Cu²⁺, so no coefficients are needed.

parts.label: c

accept: +0.59 V with a setup that does not multiply any E° by a coefficient

parts.sample: E°cell = E°(cathode) − E°(anode) = 0.34 V − (−0.25 V) = +0.59 V.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Calculate the value of ΔG° for the reaction, in kJ/mol. Include the sign.

rubric.point: Correct setup with n = 2 mol e⁻: ΔG° = −nFE° = −(2)(96,485)(0.59)
Correct answer with sign and units: −1.1 × 10² kJ/mol

parts.sample: ΔG° = −nFE° = −(2 mol e⁻)(96,485 C/mol e⁻)(0.59 V) = −1.14 × 10⁵ J/mol = −1.1 × 10² kJ/mol (−114 kJ/mol). The negative value fits a galvanic cell.

parts.label: e
parts.prompt: As the cell operates, K⁺ ions move out of the salt bridge. Identify the beaker they move into, and justify your answer.

rubric.point: K⁺ moves into Beaker 2 (the Cu half-cell), because Cu²⁺ ions are being removed there and positive charge must be replaced to keep the solution neutral
accept: into the copper beaker, to balance the loss of Cu²⁺
toward the cathode compartment because it loses cations

parts.sample: K⁺ moves into Beaker 2. Cu²⁺ ions there are reduced to Cu metal, so the solution loses positive charge; K⁺ ions replace it and keep the beaker electrically neutral.

parts.label: f
parts.prompt: The student repeats the experiment with 0.10 M Cu(NO₃)₂(aq) in Beaker 2, keeping everything else the same. Predict whether the measured cell potential will be greater than, less than or equal to the value in part (c). Justify your prediction.

rubric.point: Justification using Q: Q = [Ni²⁺]/[Cu²⁺] = 1.0/0.10 = 10 > 1, so E < E°
accept: lower reactant concentration makes Q > 1, so the cell potential falls
Q increases above 1, so E is below E°

parts.sample: The potential will be less than 0.59 V. Cu²⁺ is a reactant, so Q = [Ni²⁺]/[Cu²⁺] = 1.0/0.10 = 10. With Q > 1, the reaction has less drive than under standard conditions, so E < E°.

parts.label: g
parts.prompt: The original cell delivers a steady current of 0.150 A for 2.00 hours. Calculate the mass of copper deposited on the copper electrode.

accept: correct charge and conversion with F

rubric.point: Mass with 2 mol e⁻ per mol Cu: 0.356 g Cu
accept: consistent with an incorrect mol e⁻ carried forward correctly
